premise: By the lander, Astronaut bets Geologist his heavy hammer will land before her paper map; they drop them together — and it's a tie.
inspiration: The old riddle 'which falls faster, a feather or a stone?', answered on the Moon.
learning: With no air in the way, a hammer and a sheet of paper fall at exactly the same speed.

en-US.title: The Hammer and the Map
en-US.text: {lander:enter} {lander:go to pad} The lander stood on its pad, gold and shiny. {astronaut:enter} {astronaut:go to lander} Astronaut held up her paper map. {geologist:enter} {geologist:go to lander} Geologist held up his heavy hammer. [curious] Which one will land first? asked Astronaut. {geologist:face happy} My hammer, of course. Heavy things fall faster. Want to bet? The loser polishes the lander. {astronaut:face happy} {astronaut:hop} Deal. They held them out, side by side. Three, two, one… drop! {geologist:face surprised} {astronaut:face surprised} The hammer and the map fell together — and landed at exactly the same moment. On Earth, the air would catch the paper and float it down slowly. But the Moon has no air to get in the way. {lander:live} The lander's hatch swung open. {pilot:enter} {pilot:face happy} [laughs] A tie! said Pilot. So they both polished the lander. {geologist:live} Geologist tapped the gold with his hammer, just to check.

es-ES.title: El martillo y el mapa
es-ES.text: {lander:enter} {lander:go to pad} El módulo lunar estaba en su plataforma, dorado y reluciente. {astronaut:enter} {astronaut:go to lander} Astronauta levantó su mapa de papel. {geologist:enter} {geologist:go to lander} Geólogo levantó su martillo, bien pesado. [curious] ¿Cuál llegará antes al suelo? preguntó Astronauta. {geologist:face happy} Mi martillo, claro. Lo pesado cae más rápido. ¿Apostamos? Quien pierda, saca brillo al módulo. {astronaut:face happy} {astronaut:hop} Hecho. Los sostuvieron uno al lado del otro. Tres, dos, uno… ¡ya! {geologist:face surprised} {astronaut:face surprised} El martillo y el mapa cayeron juntos… y llegaron al suelo a la vez. En la Tierra, el aire frenaría el papel y lo bajaría despacito. Pero en la Luna no hay aire que se meta por medio. {lander:live} La escotilla del módulo se abrió. {pilot:enter} {pilot:face happy} [laughs] ¡Empate! dijo Piloto. Así que los dos le sacaron brillo al módulo. {geologist:live} Geólogo le dio unos golpecitos al dorado con el martillo, por si acaso.
